title: EDR / Sysmon tamper-protection alert fired on a sensor-stop attempt
event_type: Generic EDR/tamper-protection alert schema — triggered by a local attempt to stop the Sysmon driver/service or disable the EDR sensor

fields.label: AlertName
fields.value: Tamper Protection: Security sensor service stop attempted

fields.label: ActionTaken
fields.value: Blocked — service stop denied by tamper-protection policy

callouts.explanation: Identifies which sensor component was targeted; this is the exact driver/service Part 9 warns can be stopped by anyone with sufficient local privilege, silencing every downstream Sysmon-based detection with no error.

A legitimate, signed system binary (`sc.exe`) issuing a stop command is indistinguishable by binary identity alone from routine administration — the alert has to come from the tamper-protection layer watching the target service, not from a detection on the binary itself.

Whether the product blocks the stop attempt or only logs it after the fact is the operational difference between a prevented visibility gap and a alert that arrives after the sensor already went dark.

Confirms the attempt came from a real, sufficiently privileged local account rather than a remote or unauthenticated actor, which matters for scoping the response (compromised admin credential vs. insider vs. legitimate but unapproved change).

note: Illustrative and conceptual — an invented, generic composite of the fields a working tamper-protection alert would carry, not a screenshot of any specific vendor console or captured lab event.
